snapshot.capital_scaled: ₹40 lakh–1.5 crore for 50+ animals, a chilling unit and your own milk brand
snapshot.margin_d2c: Selling direct as a branded product earns 40–60% more per litre than selling to the dairy co-operative
snapshot.margin_production: Co-operatives and collection centres pay a fixed rate based on fat and SNF
snapshot.distribution_note: Neighbourhood delivery and subscriptions sell milk easily; scaling needs cold chain

tailwinds: Buyers in cities pay a premium for fresh, unadulterated, A2 and farm-direct milk.
Paneer, ghee and curd earn more than raw milk and keep longer.
Subscription delivery apps and WhatsApp orders make direct selling easy.
Government and NABARD-linked loans support dairy units, and states offer animal insurance and subsidies.
headwinds: Feed and fodder costs have risen sharply and swing with the monsoon.
Animal health problems can wipe out a small herd's income.
Milk must be chilled within hours and delivered daily, with no days off.
Amul and other co-operatives set a low price benchmark for regular milk.
angle_2026: Urban buyers have become wary of adulterated milk and will pay much more for farm-fresh, A2 or organic milk they can trace. In 2026, the dairy businesses that do well sell direct under their own name, add ghee and paneer, and keep feed costs under control with their own fodder.
cost_basis: Estimated for a small farm of 5–10 cows or buffaloes with its own shed, selling direct in a nearby town or city, 2026 prices.

setup_costs.covers: 5–10 good-yield cows or buffaloes, depending on breed
Milking machine, bulk milk chiller or deep freezers
First months of feed, fodder seeds, silage
Glass bottles or pouches, a two-wheeler, crates

unit_economics.note: Selling to the co-operative removes delivery costs but pays much less per litre. Most small farms mix both: premium direct sales plus the co-operative for surplus.

investor_probes: What is your average yield per animal per day?
What does feed cost per litre?
How many subscribers renew every month?
What happens to milk you can't sell the same day?
bootstrap_takeaway: Start with 5 high-yield animals, sell to 50–100 subscribers, and turn surplus milk into ghee and paneer. Grow your own fodder to control costs.
sourcing_edge: Buying animals from established breeding areas and growing your own green fodder cuts costs more than anything else. Local veterinary colleges and state animal husbandry departments offer advice and vaccinations.
licences: FSSAI registration or licence depending on scale
Local panchayat or municipal permission for the shed
Pollution control consent for larger farms

hard_truths.title: No days off
hard_truths.text: Animals need feeding and milking twice a day, every day. Plan for reliable help.

hard_truths.title: Feed costs
hard_truths.text: Fodder prices rise sharply in dry years. Grow your own fodder and store silage.

hard_truths.title: Animal health
hard_truths.text: A sick animal stops producing. Budget for vets, vaccines and insurance.

hard_truths.title: Milk spoils
hard_truths.text: Unsold milk must be chilled or processed the same day. Paneer and ghee turn waste into profit.

plan_goal: The aim is 100 paying subscribers, with surplus milk turned into ghee or paneer.

plan.title: Plan
steps: Visit 3 working dairy farms and talk to their owners.
Check the local price for branded milk and what subscribers want.
Prepare a project report for a bank loan.

plan.title: Set up
steps: Build the shed and buy 5 animals.

plan.title: Sell direct
steps: Offer trial weeks to neighbours and housing societies.
Make ghee or paneer from surplus.

plan.title: Review the numbers
steps: Calculate cost per litre and profit.
Plan your fodder supply for the year.
Decide whether to add animals or products.
